$Comment: What a player sees and hears when a quest's rewards are paid to them.
It fires both for a quest that pays out the instant it finishes and for one the player came
back to collect. 'collected' tells them apart (true for the collect), which is what the
Variants entry below reads: a quest that settled on the spot already had its quest.completed
notice, so only a collect is announced here, with the chest sound below.
This is the library's own neutral default. A mod that ships a file with this same name in its
own pack replaces it, and a server owner can do the same from the owner layer.
The moment carries 'quest' (its id), 'title' (its name in the reader's language),
'collected', the outcome as 'granted' / 'queued' / 'failed' reward counts, and 'rewards'
(what the payout actually put in the player's hands, one entry per thing). 'player' is
always the name of who was paid. The Variants entry's Sound is collecting's jingle, the
legendary chest opening. It plays on every Collect, wherever the toast shows or whether it shows
at all, and the Collect button's own toast on a quest page or a board stays silent, so a press is
one sound.
PlayerLevel true hands the toast to each player's own notification level, chosen on their
Settings tab: Every update, Milestones, Finishes or None. A variant replaces the whole toast,
so it says PlayerLevel again. Delete it to show the toast as written whatever they chose.
A quest the player can see on their quest tracker shows none of these toasts in the corner,
at any level, since the tracker already says it; drawn into an open page they still show,
and the sound still plays.
Tone colours the whole notification, frame and words together - gold Reward here, because
this moment is a payout. What was just paid lists itself as rows under the headline on the
in-page toast: a loot table shows the items it rolled rather than its name, and a roll that
landed nothing adds no row. The Toast's Rows group switches the rows off or caps how many
show.
